title: The desktop CSP hard-pins the daemon at :7717 the console lets you move
premise_notes: Verified: tauri.conf.json:24 CSP literally 127.0.0.1:7717 for media-src/connect-src; config.ts:18-21 ?daemon= > VITE_DAEMON_URL > DEFAULT; rpc.ts:7 DEFAULT_DAEMON_URL; daemon config.rs:193/205 port default 7717 and cli.rs:85 --port; errors.ts:76 and States.tsx:48 literal --port 7717; lib.rs:6-11 bare Builder; three readDataConfig call sites; ci.yml:51 src-tauri not built. Security: the daemon binds 127.0.0.1 only; the card restricts the derived endpoint to loopback hosts, emits exactly one origin (no wildcard), keeps the default CSP byte-identical and makes a non-loopback/malformed override a hard stop - so the CSP stays pinned to a single loopback origin chosen by whoever already controls the process launch. Not a widening; policy-neutral.
floor_notes: M, 8 files, 6 cases, risk 6, gate architecture (not policy-loosen per the loopback analysis). No restatement elsewhere in cards/. Write-set gap: 'an Err shows a blocking message dialog' needs tauri-plugin-dialog (src-tauri/Cargo.toml has only tauri + opener) and Cargo.toml is not in the write set - adding a plugin would also grow the shell's capability surface.
ambition_why: A real single-source-of-truth seam for the endpoint, but it serves a non-default-port scenario of modest frequency; impact 8 is generous.
grounding_why: Every cited literal and the absent shell seam are as stated.
falsifiability_why: Byte-for-byte default CSP, exact precedence, loopback refusal and port-in-hint cases are all red today and would catch a widened or wrong build.
revision: Replace the blocking message dialog with: on Err, print the source and rule to stderr and exit 1 (no new tauri plugin, no Cargo.toml change).
reason: Grounded, loopback-pinned so policy-neutral; remove the unlisted dialog-plugin dependency.

title: check-bundle says a route is over, never which chunk grew: diff vs measured
premise_notes: Verified: check-bundle.mjs:43-57 measure() sums per-chunk sizes and discards them; :80-90 prints one total row and 'js N B > budget M B'; budgets/bundle.json $comment carries hand-computed before/after figures; dist manifest shared keys carry hashes (_Button-DSPKYARD.js etc.); vite.config.ts:13 include src/** only; git log on bundle.json shows the five cited hand re-measure commits.
floor_notes: M, 6 files, 6 cases, effort 5 / impact 7 / risk 4 - all at the floor. Report-only baseline keeps the verdict deterministic. No restatement (console-quality-gates A is perf registry, contract-package A is door chunk size). Gap: chunkKey strips the hash, but Vite routinely emits several distinct shared chunks with the same stem (e.g. _index-AAAA.js and _index-BBBB.js); none collide in today's manifest (40 shared keys, 0 stem collisions), but no case guards it and a collision would silently merge two chunks' bytes.
ambition_why: Useful developer-tooling compare mode that kills hand arithmetic, but it is report ergonomics on an existing gate.
grounding_why: The discarded per-chunk figures and the hand-attributed budget raises are exactly as cited.
falsifiability_why: Synthetic-manifest cases with exact deltas are red today and pin exit codes; the stem-collision path is untested.
revision: Add an acceptance case: a manifest with two distinct shared chunks _index-AAAA.js and _index-BBBB.js keeps them as two separate chunk entries (disambiguated, never summed into one '_index.js').
reason: Honest M at the floors; guard the hash-stripping key against stem collisions.
